scope: Micropayments and payment channels (x402 and MPP lineage)
Card payment security (TAP and Agent Pay context)
Protocol analyses and recent papers (part c additions)

entries.title: zkLLM: Zero Knowledge Proofs for Large Language Models
entries.summary: Presents zkLLM, a zero-knowledge proof system specialized for large language model inference, with a parallel lookup argument for non-arithmetic tensor operations and a dedicated proof for attention. It lets a model owner prove that an output came from committed parameters without revealing them.
entries.whyItMatters: ERC-8004 leaves room for validators that check agent work with cryptographic proofs; zkLLM shows what a zkML validation response could attest to and how costly that proof is for transformer models.

entries.title: Scaling up Trustless DNN Inference with Zero-Knowledge Proofs
entries.summary: Builds the first ZK-SNARK proof of correct inference for a full-resolution ImageNet model, so a client can check after the fact that a machine learning service ran the promised model. It also sketches protocols that use these proofs to verify model accuracy and to pay for verified predictions.
entries.whyItMatters: An early, concrete answer to the question an ERC-8004 validator asks: did the service actually run the model it claimed, and can that be checked without trusting the server.

entries.title: Intel SGX Explained
entries.summary: A long technical analysis of Intel Software Guard Extensions built from Intel papers, manuals, a tutorial and patents. It explains enclave creation, memory protection and remote attestation, and it catalogs the side-channel and design weaknesses that limit the trust these guarantees deserve.
entries.whyItMatters: TEE attestation is one of the validation methods ERC-8004 anticipates; this paper is the standard reference for what an SGX attestation proves and where it does not hold.

entries.title: opML: Optimistic Machine Learning on Blockchain
entries.summary: Proposes opML, which runs machine learning inference for blockchains under an optimistic model: results are accepted unless a challenger wins an interactive fraud-proof game, similar to optimistic rollups. The authors argue this is far cheaper than zero-knowledge proofs and can serve large models on ordinary hardware.
entries.whyItMatters: Shows the crypto-economic alternative to zkML for ERC-8004 validation, where validators stake on a result and disputes, not proofs, keep inference honest.

entries.title: The Millicent Protocol for Inexpensive Electronic Commerce
entries.venue: Fourth International World Wide Web Conference (WWW4)
entries.summary: Describes Millicent, a protocol for web purchases below one cent in which brokers sell vendor-specific scrip that each vendor can validate locally, without extra network round trips or heavy cryptography. Brokers handle accounts and billing so vendors and customers do not need direct financial relationships.
entries.whyItMatters: The direct ancestor of pay-per-request web payments: x402 and MPP revisit the same goal of charging tiny amounts per HTTP resource, with stablecoins and facilitators in the broker role.

entries.title: PayWord and MicroMint: Two simple micropayment schemes
entries.summary: Introduces two micropayment schemes: PayWord, where a user commits to a hash chain and pays by revealing successive hash values, and MicroMint, where coins are hash collisions that are cheap to verify but costly to mint at scale. Both aim to make each payment far cheaper than a public-key signature.
entries.whyItMatters: The hash-chain idea behind PayWord is the template for streaming and session payments; MPP sessions and payment channels used with x402 apply the same principle of one setup and many cheap increments.

entries.title: Electronic lottery tickets as micropayments
entries.summary: Proposes paying for many small items with electronic lottery tickets: each ticket wins a larger payment with small probability, so the expected value equals the price while the number of real transactions drops sharply.
entries.whyItMatters: Probabilistic payment is one of the standing answers to per-request fees that are smaller than settlement cost, a problem x402 and MPP face whenever an agent buys thousands of cheap API calls.

entries.title: The Case Against Micropayments
entries.summary: Argues from pricing history that people prefer flat-rate and bundled pricing over metered charges, and that the mental cost of deciding on each tiny payment is the main obstacle to micropayments, not the technology.
entries.whyItMatters: The classic objection to pay-per-use pricing; agent payments may sidestep it because software, not a person, makes each spending decision, which is the core bet behind x402 and MPP.

entries.title: Micropayments for Decentralized Currencies
entries.summary: Adapts probabilistic micropayments to decentralized currencies such as Bitcoin, designing schemes where a payer issues lottery-style tickets and only winning tickets are settled on chain, with protections against a payer who double-spends the escrow.
entries.whyItMatters: Links the 1990s micropayment literature to blockchain settlement, the setting in which x402 operates and in which MPP offers on-chain payment methods.

entries.title: The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments
entries.summary: The white paper (draft version 0.5.9.2, dated 2016-01-14) for a network of bidirectional payment channels in which transfers happen off chain and are routed across channels with hashed timelock contracts, so only channel opening and closing touch the blockchain.
entries.whyItMatters: Payment channels are the main route to cheap, fast repeated payments; the deferred and session schemes discussed for x402 and MPP inherit the channel model this paper popularized.

entries.title: Sprites and State Channels: Payment Networks that Go Faster than Lightning
entries.summary: Proposes Sprites, a payment channel construction for smart-contract chains that cuts the worst-case time collateral is locked along a multi-hop route and supports partial deposits and withdrawals without closing the channel. It also gives a modular treatment of general state channels.
entries.whyItMatters: A key reference for channel designs on Ethereum-style chains, where x402 settles; it explains the collateral and dispute costs any channel-based agent payment scheme must budget for.

entries.title: Blind Signatures for Untraceable Payments
entries.summary: Introduces blind signatures, where a signer signs a message without seeing it, and uses them to build payments that the bank can verify but cannot link back to the payer.
entries.whyItMatters: The origin of private digital cash; it frames the privacy trade-off in agent payments, where x402 settles on public ledgers and card-based agent payments expose purchase data to the networks.
